paragraphs.text: Lesson 12. Shopping
Today's lesson is all about shopping.
Let's begin by learning about the different types of stores.
At a supermarket or grocery store,
you can buy food as well as things for your house, like cleaning supplies.
At a bakery, you can buy bread, cakes, pies, pastries, muffins, and cupcakes.
At a delicatessen, or deli for short,
you can buy cheese, sliced meat for sandwiches, salads, and other prepared food that is ready to eat.
At a pharmacy or drug store, you can buy medicine, band-aids, eye drops, and other personal care items.
At a florist, you can buy a bouquet of flowers.
At a jewelry store or jeweler, you can buy necklaces, bracelets, earrings, and rings.
At a pet shop, you can buy animals, like puppies, kittens, rabbits, fish, or birds.
Pet shops also sell accessories like these,
color, leash, cage, tank, bowl, and toys.
At a bookshop or bookstore, you can buy books and sometimes magazines or newspapers.
At a hardware store, you can buy things for construction or fixing things around the house,
like tools, paint, plumbing supplies, and electrical supplies.
A department store is a large store with many different areas, for example clothes, electronics, food, toys, items for the house, etc.
A mall or shopping center is a large building that contains many different stores,
usually including a food court with many different restaurants.
A convenience store or corner store is a small store that contains some basic snacks, drinks, and supplies.
Many gas stations have a convenience store, for example.
Other types of stores are often identified by the items they sell.
A toy store sells toys, a shoe store sells shoes, etc.
Let's focus on two common situations, shopping for clothes and shopping at the supermarket.
Conversation number one, shopping for clothes.
Do you need any help?
Yes, I'm looking for polo shirts.
Okay, we have a few different styles.
This one's more dressy and this one's more casual.
Can I try these on?
Sure, the fitting rooms are right over there.
How were they?
I like this casual shirt, but it's too loose.
Do you have it in a smaller size?
Let me check.
Yes, we do.
Here's a medium.
Was it okay?
It fits perfectly, but do you have it in green instead of blue?
One moment.
Here's a dark green and a light green.
I like the dark green one.
How much is it?
Normally $39.95, but it's on sale for $29.95.
I'll take it.
Conversation vocabulary and phrases.
When you go into a store, a sales person might ask, can I help you?
Or do you need any help?
To say no, you can respond.
No thanks, I'm just looking.
Or, no thanks, I'm just browsing.
The word browsing means to look through many items in a casual way.
If you want to say yes, you can respond, yes, I'm looking for, and then name the item you
want to buy.
For example, yes, I'm looking for a white dress.
Yes, I'm looking for a jacket for my son.
If you need help in finding an item in the store, you can ask a sales person.
Excuse me, where can I find children's clothing?
Excuse me, do you have any workout clothes?
Let's say you find a piece of clothing you like, but you want to put on the clothing to
see if it's the right size.
You can ask the sales person, can I try it on?
Or, where are the fitting rooms?
Or, try on rooms?
If the clothing is too big, you can say, it's too loose.
Do you have this in a smaller size?
If the clothing is too small, you can say, it's too tight.
Do you have this in a larger size?
And if the size of the clothing is correct, then you can say, it fits perfectly.
Sometimes the size is correct, but it just doesn't look good on you.
In this case, you can say, it's not my color, or it's not my style.
Finally, the phrase, I'll take it, means you are going to buy the item.
Conversation number two, returning an item.
Fred bought a jacket too, but then discovered a defect.
Listen to this conversation as he goes back to the store to return the jacket.
Hi there, I bought this jacket earlier today, but when I got home, I found out that it has
a hole in the sleeve.
Can I exchange it for another one?
Mm-hmm.
Do you have the receipt?
Yes, here you go.
Oh, I'm so sorry, but we don't have any more of that model.
Would you prefer to receive a refund or store credit?
A refund.
If you need to return an item you bought to the store, always bring the receipt.
That's the piece of paper you received when you bought the item.
It's also good if the clothing still has its original tags.
The tag is the piece of paper attached to the clothing that has the price and the barcode.
When you return an item, many stores will offer you two or three options.
You can exchange the item for another one.
This is usually done if you discover that the item is defective, meaning there is some problem with the item.
You can get a refund.
That means you get your money back.
Sometimes you can get store credit.
That means you get the price of the returned item, discounted from the next purchase you make in the store in the future.
Conversation number three, shopping at a supermarket.
When you go into the supermarket, you'll take a shopping cart or a basket if you only want to buy a few things.
Let's look at a conversation with an employee of the store.
Excuse me, where can I find the mayonnaise?
It's on aisle 12.
Okay, thanks. And do you have any non-fat yogurt?
Yes, in the dairy section.
Right, one more thing. I couldn't find any whole wheat pasta.
Sorry, we're out of it. You can check back on Monday.
Oh, okay. What about some flour seeds?
Ah, we don't carry some flour seeds. You might try the natural food store across the street.
Alright, by the way, are these boxes of cereal on sale?
Yep, they're buy one, get one free.
Great. At the checkout.
Do you have a loyalty card?
No.
Would you like to join our loyalty program? You'll get an instant 10% off this purchase.
No thanks, maybe another time. I'm in a bit of a hurry today.
Oh, that reminds me. I have a coupon for half price on these canned soups.
Alright, it comes to $152.74. How would you like to pay?
Do you take credit cards?
Yes, we do.
Here you go.
Please sign here, and here's your receipt.
Have a nice day.
Thanks, you too.
Conversation vocabulary and phrases.
To ask an employee of the store for help, you can say,
Where can I find the mayonnaise?
Do you have any non-fat yogurt?
The employee might refer you to an aisle.
Isles are the corridors in the supermarket.
Or they might tell you to go to one of these sections of the store.
The dairy section contains milk, yogurt, butter, and cheese.
The produce section has fresh fruits and vegetables.
The frozen food section has ice cream and pre-prepared meals.
The bakery sells bread, muffins, and cakes.
The deli sells sliced meat and cheese for sandwiches.
And the ethnic food section sells international and imported foods.
If the store doesn't have the item, the employee will say,
Sorry, it's out of stock at the moment.
Or, Sorry, we're out of it at the moment.
This means the item is temporarily unavailable.
Or, Sorry, we don't carry mango juice.
We don't carry means the store never sells the item.
You need to go to a different store.
You can buy food in different types of packaging.
For example, a can of soup.
A jar of jelly or jam.
A box of cereal.
A package of pasta.
A carton of milk.
A bottle of wine.
A loaf of bread.
Here are some phrases for talking about discounts.
Is this on sale?
I have a coupon.
It's 20% off.
It's buy one, get one free.
If you buy two, you get the third one free.
When you're ready to pay, go to the checkout.
The person who works there is called the cashier.
The cashier might say, How would you like to pay?
You can answer, In cash, or with a credit card.
Or with a debit card.
If you pay with a credit card, the cashier will say, Please sign here.
You should write your name on the paper.
If you pay with the debit card, the cashier will say, Please enter your pen.
Your pen is your personal identification number.
If you pay in cash, imagine your purchase's total $70 and you pay $100 in cash,
the cashier will give you back the extra money, $30, and say, Here's your change.
Or your change is $30.
Finally, the cashier will say, Here's your receipt.
Remember that the receipt is the piece of paper with the list of what you bought.
You've finished lesson 12.
Now take the quiz to test your memory of the shopping phrases.
